Coffee origins series, part 3: Ethiopia 🇪🇹

Ethiopia is widely considered the birthplace of coffee. Legend says a goat herder named Kaldi noticed his goats dancing after eating red berries from a certain shrub. Today, Ethiopian coffees are prized for their bright acidity and floral, tea-like character.

Our current single origin comes from the Guji zone, grown at 2,000 metres by a cooperative of 400 smallholder farmers. Expect jasmine, bergamot and ripe peach.
